terms.grammar: adverb, with numbers and times; also a preposition with the accusative
evidence: Caes. B.G. 2.2: diēbus circiter quīndecim ad fīnēs Belgārum pervenit (Lewis & Short)
Caes. B.G. 4.23: hōrā diēī circiter quārtā (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The plain word with a number or an hour. It stands before or after the numeral.

terms.grammar: adverb, usually after the word it qualifies
terms.comment: The readers’ word in quattuor ferē hōrārum.
With a numeral: ad ducentōs, some two hundred.

phrases.latin: diēbus circiter quīndecim ad fīnēs Belgārum pervenit
phrases.english: in about fifteen days he reached the territory of the Belgae

sources: Lewis & Short: circiter · Lewis & Short: fere
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 102.
